mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-01.title: Parity
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-01.body:
An odd difference means one prime is even, so it is 2. The other is $2 + 27 = 29$, which is prime. Sum: $2 + 29 = 31$.

**Answer: 31**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-04.title: Scale the 3-4-5
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-04.body:
The 3-4-5 triangle has perimeter 12, so the scale factor is 3: sides 9, 12, 15. Area $= \frac12 \cdot 9 \cdot 12 = 54$ in².

**Answer: 54 in²**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-04.title: Area scales by the square
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-04.body:
The 3-4-5 triangle has area 6. Lengths scale by $36/12 = 3$, so areas scale by 9: $6 \cdot 9 = 54$.

**Answer: 54 in²**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-07.title: Find the square year
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-07.body:
He turns 26 between 1976 and 2026. The only perfect square in that range is $45^2 = 2025$. Born $2025 - 26 = 1999$.

**Answer: 1999**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-10.title: Multiply the factors
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-10.body:
She pays $0.7 \times 0.8 = 0.56$ of the original price, i.e. 56%.

**Answer: 56 percent**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-10.title: Start from 100 dollars
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-10.body:
\$100 → \$70 after 30% off → \$70 − \$14 = \$56 after another 20% off. So 56%.

**Answer: 56 percent**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-11.title: Compute both times
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-11.body:
Brendan: $480 \div 60 = 8$ min. Alisa: $480 \div 80 = 6$ min. Difference: 2 minutes.

**Answer: 2 minutes**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-13.title: Count days then adjust
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-13.body:
Tuesday 3 p.m. to Friday 3 p.m. is $3 \times 24 = 72$ hours; 9 a.m. is 6 hours earlier: $72 - 6 = 66$.

**Answer: 66 hours**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-14.title: Each product is 1
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-14.body:
Every product is $(-1)(-1) = 1$. Each uses 4 consecutive numbers, so there are $100 \div 4 = 25$ products. Sum: 25.

**Answer: 25**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-16.title: Right triangle
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-16.body:
The legs are vertical (from $y = -2$ to $4$: length 6) and horizontal (from $x = -5$ to $7$: length 12). Area $= \frac12 \cdot 6 \cdot 12 = 36$.

**Answer: 36 units²**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-17.title: Fix Kaleia's section
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-17.body:
Whatever section Kaleia gets, Allison lands in that particular section with probability $\frac19$.

**Answer: $\frac{1}{9}$**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-17.title: Count pairs
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-17.body:
Kaleia: 7 choices, Allison: 9, total 63 equally likely pairs. Same section: 7. $\frac{7}{63} = \frac19$.

**Answer: $\frac{1}{9}$**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-19.title: Write it out
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-19.body:
1, 4, 5, 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, … (after the third term each term doubles). Greatest under 100: 80.

**Answer: 80**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-20.title: Convert and adjust
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-20.body:
Charlie: 72 in. Amanda: $72 - 5 = 67$ in. Max: $67 + 10 = 77$ in.

**Answer: 77 inches**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-22.title: Altitude to the base
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-22.body:
The altitude from $A$ bisects $BC$: $h = \sqrt{17^2 - 8^2} = \sqrt{225} = 15$. Area $= \frac12 \cdot 16 \cdot 15 = 120$ m².

**Answer: 120 m²**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-23.title: GCF and LCM
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-23.body:
GCF $= 2$. LCM of 8 and 6 (covers 2 and 4) $= 24$. Sum: 26.

**Answer: 26**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-24.title: Scale step by step
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-24.body:
10 bakers: 4 cakes in 3 h. 5 bakers: 4 cakes in 6 h. 5 bakers: 8 cakes in 12 h.

**Answer: 12 hours**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-24.title: Baker-hours
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-24.body:
4 cakes take $10 \cdot 3 = 30$ baker-hours, so 8 cakes take 60 baker-hours. With 5 bakers: $60 \div 5 = 12$ h.

**Answer: 12 hours**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-26.title: Exponent must be an integer
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-26.body:
$\left(7^{1/4}\right)^n = 7^{n/4}$. For $n = 1, 2, 3$ this is $\sqrt[4]{7}, \sqrt7, \sqrt[4]{343}$, all irrational (7 is not a perfect square or fourth power). For $n = 4$ it is 7.

**Answer: 4**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-27.title: Shared side
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-27.body:
Pentagon side $= 65 \div 5 = 13$ cm, which is also the triangle's side. Triangle perimeter $= 3 \cdot 13 = 39$ cm.

**Answer: 39 cm**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-28.title: Equation
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-28.body:
With $n$ tests total, a perfect final gives $\frac{90(n-1) + 100}{n} = 92$, so $90n + 10 = 92n$ and $n = 5$.

**Answer: 5 tests**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-28.title: Spread the surplus
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-28.body:
A 100 on the final is 10 points above the current 90 average. Spread over all $n$ tests it raises the average by $\frac{10}{n} = 2$, so $n = 5$.

**Answer: 5 tests**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-31.title: Count edges
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-31.body:
Area $m = 8$. Each square has 4 edges ($32$ in all); each of the 7 edges shared by two squares removes 2 from the perimeter: $n = 32 - 14 = 18$. $m + n = 26$.

**Answer: 26**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-33.title: Independent events
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-33.body:
Each is born on a Tuesday with probability $\frac17$: $\frac17 \cdot \frac17 = \frac{1}{49}$.

**Answer: $\frac{1}{49}$**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-34.title: Elimination
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-34.body:
Double the second: $6x + 4y = 14$. Subtract the first: $x = 5$. Then $15 + 2y = 7$, so $y = -4$.

**Answer: −4**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-35.title: Cheapest per ounce
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-35.body:
Math Mart costs about 15¢ per ounce, Solvers' about 23¢, so buy Math Mart: $6 \times 2.99 = 17.94$ dollars buys 120 fl oz; the leftover \$2.06 buys nothing. Any swap to Solvers' costs \$4 more for only 10 more ounces, and $20 - 6.99 = 13.01$ allows just 4 Math Marts ($80 + 30 = 110$ oz). Maximum: 120 fl oz.

**Answer: 120 fl oz**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-36.title: No need for the scores
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-36.body:
A new score 10 above the current mean raises the mean by $\frac{10}{5} = 2$ points.

**Answer: 2 points**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-36.title: Compute
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-36.body:
Sum $= 83.6$, mean $= 20.9$, fifth score $= 30.9$. New mean $= \frac{114.5}{5} = 22.9$, up by 2.

**Answer: 2 points**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-39.title: Perfect square
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-39.body:
The sum of the first $n$ odd numbers is $n^2$: $10^2 = 100$.

**Answer: 100**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-43.title: Triangle inequality
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-43.body:
The walk home $d$ satisfies $350 - 200 \le d \le 350 + 200$, i.e. $150 \le d \le 550$ (extremes when the three places are in a line). The total varies by $550 - 150 = 400$ ft.

**Answer: 400 feet**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-44.title: Distance times fraction
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-44.body:
The distance is $39 - (-17) = 56$; $\frac34$ of it is 42. $-17 + 42 = 25$.

**Answer: 25**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-45.title: Count in groups
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-45.body:
For each penny there are 5 nickels and 10 dimes: $1 + 25 + 100 = 126$ cents per group. $882 \div 126 = 7$ groups, so $5 \times 7 = 35$ nickels.

**Answer: 35 nickels**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-47.title: Multiples of 12
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-47.body:
The number is a multiple of 4 and 6, hence of 12, and leaves remainder 4 when divided by 5. $12 \to 2$, $24 \to 4$ ✓.

**Answer: 24 dog walks**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-48.title: Push values up
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-48.body:
Make the two smallest as big as possible: both at most 100 (the median), so the smallest is 100 and the largest is $100 + 10 = 110$. List: 100, 100, 100, 110, 110. Mean $= \frac{520}{5} = 104$.

**Answer: 104**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-49.title: Close the gap
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-49.body:
The gap starts at $47 - 15 = 32$ and shrinks by 3 each day. After $k$ days Mac is ahead when $3k > 32$, i.e. $k = 11$. Eleven days after Monday is $11 = 7 + 4$: Monday + 4 = Friday. (Day 11: Mac 70, Millie 69.)

**Answer: Friday**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-51.title: Midpoint and slope
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-51.body:
Midpoint $(2, 3)$; the segment's slope is 1, so the bisector has slope $-1$: $y - 3 = -(x - 2)$, i.e. $y = -x + 5$. $y$-intercept: $(0, 5)$.

**Answer: (0, 5)**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-51.title: Equidistant points
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-51.body:
A point $(0, y)$ on the bisector is equally far from both endpoints: $1 + (y - 2)^2 = 9 + (y - 4)^2 \Rightarrow -4y + 5 = -8y + 25 \Rightarrow y = 5$.

**Answer: (0, 5)**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-52.title: Round up
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-52.body:
Relatives must bake $35 - 6 = 29$ dozen: $29 \div 2 = 14.5$, so 15 relatives. With Alyx: 16 bakers.

**Answer: 16 bakers**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-55.title: Expand
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-55.body:
$(2x + 3)(3x + 5) = 6x^2 + 19x + 15$. The coefficients are 6 and 19 (15 is the constant term): $6 + 19 = 25$.

**Answer: 25**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-57.title: Greedy
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-57.body:
4 quarters (\$1.00), 1 dime, 1 nickel, 3 pennies: $4 + 1 + 1 + 3 = 9$ coins. The 3 pennies are forced (value ≡ 3 mod 5), and 15 cents need at least 2 coins.

**Answer: 9 coins**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-59.title: Reduce the ratio
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-59.body:
20 oranges = 26 bananas in cost, so 10 oranges = 13 bananas. Since $\gcd(10, 13) = 1$, this is the smallest: $10 + 13 = 23$ pieces.

**Answer: 23 pieces**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-61.title: Fractions per week
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-61.body:
Together they save $\frac15 + \frac16 = \frac{11}{30}$ of the price per week. After 2 weeks: $\frac{22}{30} < 1$; after 3 weeks: $\frac{33}{30} \ge 1$. So 3 weeks.

**Answer: 3 weeks**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-64.title: Units digit 6
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-64.body:
$46^{2026}$ ends in the same digit as $6^{2026}$, and every power of 6 ends in 6.

**Answer: 6**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-65.title: Positions from 12
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-65.body:
Minute hand: $20 \times 6^\circ = 120^\circ$. Hour hand: $8 \times 30^\circ + 20 \times 0.5^\circ = 250^\circ$. Angle: $250^\circ - 120^\circ = 130^\circ$.

**Answer: 130 degrees**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-66.title: Average the equations
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-66.body:
$2x - y$ is the average of $x - y$ and $3x - y$: $\frac{15 + 71}{2} = 43$.

**Answer: 43**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-67.title: Volume ∝ depth
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-67.body:
Depth is multiplied by $1.5$, so volume is too: $42 \times 1.5 = 63$ in³.

**Answer: 63 in³**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-71.title: Same area
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-71.body:
Area $= 12 \times 5 = 60$ cm², so the other height is $60 \div 10 = 6$ cm.

**Answer: 6 cm**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-72.title: Cross products
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-72.body:
For a rectangle cut by one horizontal and one vertical line, diagonal products are equal: shaded $\times 48 = 70 \times 120$, so shaded $= \frac{8400}{48} = 175$.

**Answer: 175 units²**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-72.title: Ratio of columns
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-72.body:
In the bottom row the right column is $\frac{120}{48} = 2.5$ times as wide as the left. Same in the top row: $70 \times 2.5 = 175$.

**Answer: 175 units²**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-77.title: Group by sets
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-77.body:
One of each coin is $1 + 5 + 10 + 25 = 41$ cents; four sets: 164 cents = \$1.64.

**Answer: \$1.64**

mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-78.title: Largest side
mathcounts-2026-chapter-countdown-78.body:
$7^2 = 49 < 50 \le 64 = 8^2$, so the side is at most 7: perimeter 28 in.

**Answer: 28 inches**
